title: Smile and Visitor
premise: Folklorist Gideon Ishikawa arrives in the frost-bound village of Hollowmere to record songs the locals refuse to sing twice, lodging with the Vane family whose mirrors begin reflecting the room one second late. He discovers the lag is a countdown: the house's founding family traded their reflections for protection from the Visitor, a thing that walks the frost lines and takes whoever the count reaches zero on. As Gideon falls in love with Mirren Vane and realizes his own reflection has begun moving independently, he must choose between completing his life's work — transcribing the forbidden song that binds the Visitor — and smuggling the family out before the final frost pattern completes. In the end Gideon stays behind as the substitute the count demands, singing the song twice himself so the family escapes; the last chapter reveals he now lives inside the mirror's one-second delay, watching them through every reflective surface, loved and lost at once.
about_author: Gideon Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist of regional ballads who spent a decade collecting songs in remote northern settlements before turning to fiction. They write horror rooted in folklore, obsessed with the idea that every tradition exists to keep something out.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He travels to Hollowmere through fog that seems to erase the road behind him, arriving at dusk with his recording equipment and a letter of invitation signed by a man the village claims died years ago. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination, the collector's hunger meeting the first wrong note.

chapters.title: A House That Counts Its Doors
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Vane family welcomes him warmly but oddly: matriarch Edith counts the doors aloud each night, young Tam refuses to look at windows after dark, and every mirror in the house faces the wall except one. Emotional beat: hospitality laced with dread.

chapters.title: The Song They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He records old Bram Vane singing a harvest lullaby; when asked for a second take, the room goes silent and Bram leaves without a word. That night Gideon plays the recording back and hears a second voice underneath, answering each line. Emotional beat: scholarly thrill curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Mirren
chapters.summary: Mirren's POV. She watches the folklorist poke at things her family has buried for generations, torn between warning him off and being drawn to the first outsider who listens properly. A walk along the frozen river establishes their connection. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Shaving at the single uncovered mirror, he notices his reflection's hand lags behind his own — a full second, then catching up. He tests it with a metronome and confirms it isn't his imagination. Emotional beat: rational denial cracking.

chapters.title: What Edith Knows
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. She confronts Gideon privately, telling him only fragments: the founding Vanes made a bargain, the count began when he arrived, and the frost writes patterns that must never be finished. She begs him to leave by Thursday. Emotional beat: protective desperation.

chapters.title: The Frost Lines
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He maps the strange geometric patterns forming in the frost on the windows and realizes they match the notation of the forbidden song exactly — the song is a map, or a cage. Emotional beat: the scholar's epiphany and its terrible implications.

chapters.title: Tam's Window
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The boy confesses to Gideon that something stands in the yard at night, patient, counting under its breath; he's heard it reach forty-one. Gideon looks and sees nothing — but the snow shows a single line of footprints ending mid-yard. Emotional beat: childhood terror shared like contraband.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Analyzing the recording, he isolates the answering voice and matches it to no living villager — but its timbre resembles his own. His reflection, meanwhile, has begun smiling when he doesn't. Emotional beat: identity beginning to slip.

chapters.title: Love Against the Leaving
chapters.summary: Mirren's POV. Mirren and Gideon admit their feelings in the seed cellar, and she tells him the whole truth: the Visitor was invited once, long ago, and can only be refused by a family member's reflection given freely. She refuses to let him become collateral. Emotional beat: love declared against duty's wall.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Fifty
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs. The whole household hears the counting voice reach fifty; every mirror in the village fogs over at once. Edith begins packing in secret, deciding to break the family out regardless of consequence. Emotional beat: communal dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The old man admits he answered the invitation letter himself, desperate for money to save the farm, not knowing what the signature would summon. He offers Gideon his own reflection instead. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Interlude: What the Mirror Sees
chapters.summary: The reflection's POV — italicized, uncanny. It watches Gideon sleep, practices his handwriting, and hums the song's melody slightly wrong on purpose. It does not hate him; it envies him. Emotional beat: cold, curious menace.

chapters.title: The Pattern Nears Completion
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Only one segment of the frost pattern remains blank, shaped precisely like a human silhouette. Gideon deciphers the final verse of the song and understands: the count ends when someone stands in the pattern's center at dawn. Emotional beat: clarity as horror.

chapters.title: Thursday Comes Early
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. The family attempts to flee before dawn, but every road loops back to Hollowmere; the car's mirrors show the house still behind them no matter how far they drive. The Visitor is not chasing them — it is keeping them. Emotional beat: hope breaking against inevitability.

chapters.title: The Bargain Rewritten
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon proposes the unthinkable: an outsider's reflection, offered freely, might satisfy the count better than blood. Edith refuses; Mirren refuses harder; Bram quietly agrees to help him anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice proposed and fought over.

chapters.title: Singing It Twice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the night kitchen, Gideon learns the song completely and sings it twice aloud — the act forbidden for two hundred years — binding himself into the pattern. The frost leaps across every window at once, writing his outline. Emotional beat: terrible agency, calm at the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Visitor at the Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The Visitor finally enters, wearing a face assembled from everyone's missing reflections, and walks the count to ninety-nine while the family huddles in the hall. It stops before Gideon and extends a courteous hand. Emotional beat: confrontation held at the edge of a heartbeat.

chapters.title: The Center of the Pattern
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. At dawn Gideon steps into the frost's final blank space and gives his reflection freely; the count reaches one hundred as the mirror-world takes him and releases the Vanes. Mirren screams his name into glass that no longer shows him. Emotional beat: devastating, transcendent loss.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Mirren's POV. The family buries an empty coffin; the roads open; spring comes early and wrong. Mirren keeps one mirror uncovered against all tradition, unable to explain why. Emotional beat: grief learning to live in the house it saved.

chapters.title: Every Reflective Surface
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, transformed. He exists in the one-second delay now, able to watch the family through any reflective surface but never touch anything. He sees Mirren leave the mirror uncovered for him, and he learns to make his presence felt as a warmth in the glass. Emotional beat: sorrow softened into devotion.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Softly
chapters.summary: Mirren's POV, resolution. Years later, Mirren teaches her daughter the lullaby and sings it twice, deliberately, ending the cycle of fear; in the window's frost, a familiar pattern blooms briefly — a smile. Some bargains, kept in love, become blessings. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, the haunting redeemed.
